purpose: Separate cross-program timing error from changes in the native host and within-executable transfer. Diagnose errors that survive every nonnegative choice of weights for the registered counters.
calibration_input: Each ELF has one calibration input identified by the original #82 case split ('calibration'). Run these seven inputs first on the new guest. The first direct native execution of each executable, its rep-0 warmup, is the only new native observation available to the anchored predictor. Record that cost once per executable. Its nine subsequent measured native times are reference-only. The #82 full calibration CPU and the instrumented child CPU are never used as native anchors.
anchors: Use the exact rational instruction-plus-total-REP work coefficients fitted to integer and REP-copy on the older #154 guest, before the current experiment. Let W be their linear sum of the same-run counters. For each of eleven held inputs use ceil(first_native_ns * W(input) / W(calibration)). For calibration use the original #82 single full run. For input use every genuinely delivered observation in the main score, including the separate executed full fallback on the two rejected controls. A nonpositive calibration work is an error. Report the unanchored ceil(W(input)), the anchor alone, and the analogous anchored prediction using the older guest's seven-run native median when the exact input and ELF match. All seven calibration inputs are excluded from these within-ELF test scores. Compare on the identical inputs and do not train a new coefficient in this analysis.
scoring: Use the median of nine subsequent native runs as the reference per held input. A case passes when every rounded prediction is within the inclusive 20% band. Separately report all real held inputs (8) and the controls (3). Evaluate implied verdicts at the exact relative millisecond boundaries of design.json, including its 1 ms floor, skipped non-straddling pairs and strict exceeds. A false timeout or false pass is counted per boundary when any prediction disagrees with a unanimous outcome across all nine native observations. Preserve individually ambiguous boundaries and all trials. Calibrating on a native execution of the same binary and input family supplies additional information and CPU cost.
guest_transfer: For every exact original-program case with seven #154 native reference samples, report historical and fresh min, median, max, the signed ratio of medians, and whether the two observed intervals intersect. Report both cohorts' duration and spread gates (minimum at least 20 ms and within-case range/median at most 10%). These are descriptive between-guest comparisons and do not establish a causal source of variation.
pair_bound: For each view (genuinely delivered, full) compute a lower bound for any additive nonnegative clock with a nonnegative intercept and the specified counter columns. Test {instructions,rep_bytes}, {instructions,rep_bytes,loads}, {instructions,rep_bytes,loads,far_pairs} and the enlarged set {instructions,movs_bytes,stos_bytes,loads,pairs,near_pairs,far_pairs,max_span_bytes}. Enumerate ordered distinct cases in the cross-family real holdouts, in all real cases (separate cross-family and within-family pools), and in both controls' combined cases. Use the minimum native time for slower A, maximum native time for faster B and most permissive feature ratio R=max(1,max_features(max(A)/min(B))). Skip pairs with positive numerator and zero denominator in any column, ignore a column identically zero across the two extrema. Affine scores satisfy score(A)<=R*score(B). Allow one nanosecond for upward rounding of score(A). Thus max relative error >= max(0,(min_native(A)-R*max_native(B)-1)/(min_native(A)+R*max_native(B))). Report the strongest bound per pool, with ties broken by increasing lexicographic ordered case IDs and exact rational arithmetic. Include a real-cases cross-family subset with both cases passing the fresh duration/spread gates. A bound is a statement about this particular family of clocks. Failure to find a positive witness is inconclusive.
